euronews.description: Wednesday's accident happened in the middle of the pre-election campaign, adding pressure to Sánchez's government. With a month to go, parties are locked in a blame battle.

euronews.description: More than a dozen EU countries are challenging Brussels' plans to favour electricity over gas, warning that the proposals would undermine national control over energy taxation and grid charges.

euronews.title: German serial rapist sentenced to 12 years as police investigate 44 more cases
euronews.description: Frank S. was sentenced to 12 years in prison, followed by preventive detention. The 69-year-old from Berlin systematically drugged and raped 14 women and filmed the assaults. A further 44 cases are expected to be examined in a separate trial.

euronews.title: Netenyahu's Likud party alleges interference and fraud in Israel's election
euronews.description: Qatar has denied interfering in the election or funding efforts to influence the result, calling the accusations “ridiculous and dangerous”.

euronews.title: Palestinian President Abbas signals readiness for talks with Israel, seeks Cyprus mediation
euronews.description: During his visit to Cyprus, the president of the Palestinian Authority Mahmoud Abbas said he is ready for talks with Israel's new government.

euronews.title: ‘I cannot remain neutral’: Lagarde finally explains her early ECB exit
euronews.description: Lagarde says she is leaving the ECB early because she can no longer stay neutral. She also revealed the ECB debated a hike and hinted at a December move.

euronews.title: Vatican: Century of Mercedes-Benz popemobiles goes on display
euronews.description: From silk-lined limousines to vehicles fitted with bulletproof glass, eight historic popemobiles go on display at the Vatican Museums. The exhibition traces how papal transport has evolved over nearly a century.

euronews.title: Europeans still worry about climate change – but are losing faith in EU green policies
euronews.description: A new international poll reveals a widening gap between concern about climate change and confidence in the policies designed to tackle it, as EU governments struggle to reconcile ambitious green targets with mounting pressure to cut energy bills.

euronews.title: Brussels hopes unspent defence loans may help plug Ukraine’s budget hole
euronews.description: The European Commission has reopened €21.3bn in unspent SAFE defence loans, urging EU governments to use them for joint projects with Ukraine, which faces a €70bn budget gap. Brussels cannot force them, but hopes the joint procurement rules will steer some of the money to Kyiv.

euronews.title: Mistral releases latest AI model for download, giving companies more control over their cybersecurity
euronews.description: The French AI company says its Large 4 model offers advanced coding and cyber-defence capabilities and can be run on an organisation’s own computers and servers.

euronews.title: ‘I’m not a candidate for anything’: What Lagarde told Euronews before quitting the ECB
euronews.description: Christine Lagarde told Euronews in an exclusive interview in July that she was not a candidate for any political office. Her announcement that she will leave the European Central Bank early, in February 2027, comes just months before France’s presidential election.

euronews.title: You Only Audition Once: Which actors came close to being cast as James Bond?
euronews.description: James Bond is one of Hollywood’s most coveted roles, and some very famous actors came close to playing 007. As we wait for the identity of the seventh actor to land the role, here's a look back at the Bonds we never got.

euronews.title: Albania: opposition MPs disrupt parliament with smoke flares
euronews.description: Opposition MPs disrupted a parliamentary session in Albania by brandishing smoke flares and displaying photographs of injured protesters. They accused police of using violence against demonstrators demanding Prime Minister Edi Rama's resignation.

euronews.title: After the victory: The foreign policy and governing challenges facing Serbia’s student movement
euronews.description: The victory of Serbia’s Student List has fundamentally changed the country’s political landscape. But winning the election may prove to have been the easier part.

rfi.title: Paris suburb shooting suspect 'targeted Muslims, Africans or North Africans'
rfi.description: The man being held over the shootings which took place last Friday in the Paris suburbs of Trappes and La Verrière – which left one man dead and several people wounded, including an 11-year-old girl – has said he specifically targeted people of Muslim, African or North African appearance, anti-terrorism investigators revealed on Thursday.

rfi.title: Real Madrid says Mbappé was wrong over Mao Zedong as China fallout continues
rfi.description: Spanish football club Real Madrid, as well as Spanish league bosses, were on Thursday waiting to see if their apologies had led to a thaw in relations with China following striker Kylian Mbappé's comments about the former Chinese leader Mao Zedong.

rfi.title: US judge narrows Macrons' defamation lawsuit against American podcaster
rfi.description: A judge in the United States has ruled that French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte ​could continue their defamation lawsuit against the companies of the American podcaster Candace Owens, but not against Owens herself.

rfi.title: Spain begins three days of national mourning after train crash kills at least 68
rfi.description: Spain on Thursday began three days of official mourning, after a rail collision south of Madrid on Wednesday killed at least 68 people and injured more than 100.

rfi.title: Russia-Africa summit tests Moscow's ambitions for broader influence
rfi.description: More than 20 African leaders are in Moscow for a summit that will test Russia's bid to expand its influence on the continent. The two-day Russia-Africa Summit, the third since 2019, comes as Moscow grapples with heavy sanctions over its Ukraine offensive – and as several African governments turn to it for security assistance.

rfi.title: Medical experts warn climate change is now a 'global health emergency'
rfi.description: The damage wreaked by climate change on human health is escalating, experts warn, with deaths from heat, drought and other extreme weather rising faster than the world is taking action to limit global warming. Published on Wednesday, a report by medical journal The Lancet calls for climate change to be declared "a global health emergency".

rfi.title: French Senate toughens proposals to make rioters pay for damage
rfi.description: The upper house of the French parliament has toughened a proposed law that would make people who participate in rioting and vandalism liable for up to €10,000, after nationwide protests against failing schools and the cost of living that turned violent in Paris and other cities. Rights groups warn the legislation could undermine the democratic right to protest.

rfi.title: Egypt's mahrganat music: from the streets to five-star hotels
rfi.description: Born in Egypt’s working-class neighbourhoods, mahraganat music is loud and raw, and these days it is practically impossible to escape. But for the artists behind it, mahraganat is more than just party music: they see it as the latest chapter in Egypt’s rich musical history.

rfi.title: Netanyahu bloc leads after half of Israeli votes counted but no majority
rfi.description: The camp of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was ahead of his rival's opposition bloc but still short of a majority on Wednesday after 50 percent of votes were counted in Israel's pivotal general election.

rfi.title: French media protest manhandling of journalists at far-right party rally
rfi.description: More than 40 French media groups, including Radio France International, have called on Marine Le Pen's far-right National Rally (RN) to allow them to work freely after journalists were allegedly subjected to rough treatment at a party congress last weekend.

rfi.title: Iraqi court jails seven French nationals over Islamic State membership
rfi.description: An Iraqi court has sentenced seven French nationals to prison for belonging to the Islamic State armed group, handing down the first verdicts in proceedings involving French detainees transferred from Syria last year.

rfi.title: Somalia reports deadly fighting with Al-Shabaab as both sides claim heavy losses
rfi.description: Somalia’s government and Al-Shabaab militants have issued sharply conflicting accounts of deadly fighting near the southern city of Leego, with both sides claiming to have inflicted heavy losses during a battle on Monday.

rfi.title: PSG bosses hail club of the year success at 2026 Ballon d'Or awards
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain president Nasser Al-Khelaïfi on Tuesday praised head coach Luis Enrique and his squad after the club retained the Ballon d’Or Club of the Year award.

rfi.title: France pledges university admissions overhaul and education funding to ease protests
rfi.description: France’s government has promised to replace Parcoursup, the university admissions platform, and to invest in schools and student support, offering a package of concessions aimed at defusing weeks of protests over education and the rising cost of living.

rfi.title: Polls open in Israel as Netanyahu faces close contest after three years of war
rfi.description: Polls opened in Israel on Tuesday in the country’s first election since the Hamas-led attack of 7 October 2023, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu facing a close contest after three years of war and deepening political divisions.

rfi.title: Macron vows to stand firm against disorder during visit to Marseille
rfi.description: President Emmanuel Macron on Monday gave his full support to security forces as France prepared for a third consecutive weekend of protests over the poor state of schools and the rising cost of living.

rfi.title: Putellas and Kane win 2026 Ballon d'Or as PSG retain men's team of year prize
rfi.description: Spain midfielder Alexia Putellas and the Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane won the 2026 women's and men's Ballon d'Or on Monday night as Paris Saint-Germain retained the men's team of the year award.

rfi.title: Senegal PM vows to address economic issues as 2026 Youth Olympics Games loom
rfi.description: Senegal's Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo on Monday promised to solve the battle over the budget between members of the ruling Pastef party as the country counts down for the start of the 2026 Youth Olympic games on Saturday.

lemonde.title: Attentat raciste de Trappes : Kevin T., mis en examen pour « assassinat et tentatives d’assassinat terroriste », a reconnu avoir ciblé des personnes « de type musulman » ou « africain »
lemonde.description: Le Parquet national antiterroriste a précisé, jeudi, que le diagnostic de schizophrénie, évoqué par le suspect, n’était pas confirmé par son médecin. Il a par ailleurs évoqué la découverte, à son domicile, de 30 autocollants confectionnés par Kevin T. portant la mention « Vive la France, RN, fier d’être français ».

lemonde.title: En Espagne, la catastrophe ferroviaire d’Urda pose à nouveau la question du développement inconsidéré des trains à grande vitesse
lemonde.description: Le débat sur le manque d’entretien présumé des voies ferrées, en regard d’investissements colossaux dans le développement du réseau, pourrait marquer un tournant dans la campagne pour les législatives du 29 novembre, à la suite de l’accident survenu mercredi 28 octobre près de Tolède, qui a fait au moins 69 morts.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, midterms 2026 : la croissance accélère à 3,4 %, l’inflation grimpe à 3,6 %, à quelques jours des élections de mi-mandat aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: Les chiffres publiés jeudi par le département du commerce américain ont montré une nette accélération de l’économie américaine cet été, avec 3,4 % de croissance du PIB en rythme annuel au troisième trimestre.

lemonde.title: Conforté par ses affaires avec Donald Trump, Vladimir Poutine compte intensifier la guerre en Ukraine
lemonde.description: Alors que les Etats-Unis multiplient les annonces d’accords dans le domaine énergétique avec la Russie, la perspective de négociations de paix consensuelles entre Kiev et Moscou ne cesse de s’éloigner.

lemonde.title: Avec « Soulèvement », Angelin Preljocaj capte les colères contemporaines
lemonde.description: Le chorégraphe signe, pour ses douze danseurs, une fresque insurrectionnelle où les corps se dressent et s’étreignent, sur une partition électro ensorcelante d’Irène Drésel.

lemonde.title: En Israël, Benyamin Nétanyahou accuse les partis arabes de fraude électorale et d’avoir reçu des fonds de l’étranger
lemonde.description: Les partis arabes sont en passe d’obtenir un score élevé aux élections législatives, qui les rend en mesure de faire pencher la balance en faveur de l’opposition. Selon ces partis, les accusations proférées à leur encontre « révèlent la peur » du premier ministre.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : les préfectures de Paris et des Hauts-de-Seine interdisent le colloque sur la « remigration » organisé par les identitaires
lemonde.description: Devant réunir des figures des mouvements identitaires européens et américains, un forum, le 31 octobre, interdit « à la demande du ministre de l’intérieur » pour des « risques de troubles publics », visait à diffuser les concepts de « remigration » et la théorie complotiste et raciste du « grand remplacement ».

lemonde.title: Pour Airbus et Boeing, la « galère » de la hausse de la production
lemonde.description: Les deux géants de l’aéronautique, en retard sur leurs promesses de livraison pour 2026, affichent des résultats en demi-teinte au troisième trimestre. Le groupe américain a même dû se résoudre à revenir sur ses objectifs officiels de cadencement industriel.

lemonde.title: « Je veux avoir la liberté de parole », dit Christine Lagarde après l’annonce de son départ de la BCE en février 2027
lemonde.description: En quittant son poste dès le début de l’année, Christine Lagarde ouvre la possibilité à Emmanuel Macron de participer à la désignation de son successeur avant l’élection présidentielle.

lemonde.title: Anticor se constitue partie civile dans l’enquête sur Edouard Philippe
lemonde.description: Comme l’a appris « Le Monde », l’association anticorruption a effectué cette démarche le 20 octobre, dans l’information judiciaire ouverte en mai par le PNF sur d’éventuels contournements des règles du marché public au Havre.

lemonde.title: En Afrique, les masculinistes ont le vent en poupe : « Défendre les droits des hommes bafoués par cette société matriarcale »
lemonde.description: « En Afrique, la vague réactionnaire » (3/4). Propagés par des influenceurs aux larges audiences, les discours masculinistes et de haine envers les femmes sont en pleine recrudescence sur le continent. Cherchant à reprendre le dessus face à un courant féministe « émasculant », cette manosphère prospère sur les crises économiques et politiques qui frappent de plein fouet les jeunesses africaines.

lemonde.title: Au Canada, quinze jeunes poursuivent l’Etat pour inaction climatique, dénonçant une « atteinte injustifiée » à leurs droits
lemonde.description: Plusieurs plaignants n’étaient que des enfants lorsqu’ils ont décidé d’attaquer l’Etat en justice, en 2019. Une bataille judiciaire qui pourrait faire date en déterminant jusqu’où un Etat est tenu de protéger ses citoyens contre le réchauffement climatique.

lemonde.title: Le Mexique soulagé de la réélection de Lula au Brésil
lemonde.description: Pour la présidente Claudia Sheinbaum et son parti de gauche, Morena, la victoire du président brésilien sortant prouve qu’il est possible d’enrayer le virage à droite et à l’extrême droite des pays de la région, malgré l’ingérence de Washington dans les processus électoraux.

lemonde.title: En Thaïlande, le combat solitaire du lanceur d’alerte Yingcheep Atchanont contre la fraude électorale
lemonde.description: L’ONG iLaw du juriste Yingcheep Atchanont a rendu publique le 21 octobre l’intégralité du dossier d’enquête sur une fraude massive aux élections sénatoriales de juin 2024, après que la Commission électorale thaïlandaise a écarté de toute poursuite les principaux suspects, dont le premier ministre, Anutin Charnvirakul.

lemonde.title: La NASA accélère son plan de vol pour retourner sur la Lune dès 2028, un pari risqué
lemonde.description: L’agence spatiale américaine a annoncé un calendrier resserré et ambitieux de son programme lunaire. La prochaine mission, Artemis-3, pourrait avoir lieu à l’été 2027, avant deux alunissages en 2028, dernière année du mandat de Donald Trump.

france24fr.title: Midterms : Barack Obama, le joker des démocrates de la dernière heure
france24fr.description: L’ex-président démocrate Barack Obama a participé en une semaine à trois grands rassemblements de campagne pour les élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis. Au fil des ans, il semble être devenu le joker du camp démocrate dans la dernière ligne droite avant un scrutin. Ce n’est pas un hasard.

france24fr.title: Le sport espagnol rend hommage aux victimes de la collision entre deux trains

france24fr.title: Législatives en Israël : accusations de fraude envers le parti arabe, le président appelle au calme

france24fr.title: Guerre en Ukraine : une frappe russe tue 13 personnes à la gare centrale de Dnipro
france24fr.description: Une attaque de drone russe a tué treize personnes jeudi 29 octobre à la ​gare ‌centrale de Dnipro, dans l'est ⁠de l'Ukraine, en touchant un quai ‌bondé de voyageurs qui s'apprêtaient à monter ⁠dans un train. france24fr.title: Midterms : la Maison Blanche s'apprête-t-elle à conetster les résultats en cas d'echec ?
france24fr.description: À l'approche des midterms qui se dérouleront mardi 3 novembre 2026 aux États-Unis, les sondages indiquent 36 % d'opinion favorable au président ultra conservateur, Donald Trump. france24fr.title: Accident ferroviaire en Espagne : le roi Felipe XI présent aux chevets des victimes
france24fr.description: Le roi d'Espagne Felipe VI a réclamé jeudi 29 octobre des "mesures" pour éviter une nouvelle catastrophe ferroviaire, au lendemain de la collision de deux trains qui a tué au moins 69 personnes et en a blessé une centaine. france24fr.description: Les victimes du massacre d’El-Fasher témoignent des atrocités subies, un an après le massacre. france24fr.title: Restauration de la nature : l'ONU appelle le monde à accélérer la cadence
france24fr.description: Une restauration sans précédent des écosystèmes est à l’œuvre à travers le monde. Mais elle ne va pas assez vite. C’est ce que montre un rapport de l’ONU publié alors que la COP17 sur la biodiversité, à Erevan, en Arménie, touche à sa fin.

france24fr.title: En France, deux événements d'extrême droite radicale interdits par les autorités

france24fr.title: Changement climatique : une “urgence sanitaire mondiale”, alertent des chercheurs

france24fr.description: Le Niger estime que son voisin, le Tchad, est responsable de la mort de deux civils sur son territoire, suite à une frappe de drone survenue le 24 octobre dernier. nzz.description: Nachdem Rechtsextreme zu Protesten gegen das Zürcher Konzert des deutschen Rappers aufgerufen hatten, war die Nervosität gross. Der Künstler selbst nahm es aber gelassen und lancierte spontan einen «Spendenlauf».

spiegel.title: Ahrtal-Katastrophe 2021: Eltern von Flutopfer legen Verfassungsbeschwerde ein
spiegel.description: Die 22 Jahre alte Johanna Orth starb in der Ahrtalflut 2021. Ihre Eltern fordern eine strafrechtliche Aufarbeitung der Katastrophe und wenden sich dafür nun an das Bundesverfassungsgericht.

spiegel.title: Alphabet-Aktie: Schwächeres Wachstum in Google-Kerngeschäft alarmiert US-Markt
spiegel.description: Investoren haben auf enttäuschende Zahlen des Google-Mutterkonzerns reagiert: Die Alphabet-Aktie brach um mehr als zwölf Prozent ein – und steuert damit auf einen Rekordverlust zu.

spiegel.title: Alaska prüft Klage wegen zwei gleich heißender Midterms-Kandidaten
spiegel.description: Dan S. Sullivan oder Dan J. Sullivan? In Alaska heißen zwei Kandidaten für die Senatswahl nahezu gleich. Die Republikaner verdächtigen die Demokraten, hinter den Verwirrspiel zu stehen. Jetzt schaltet sich der Gouverneur ein.

spiegel.title: Christina Block: Gericht in Dänemark spricht Kindern 63.000 Euro Unterhalt zu
spiegel.description: Ein dänisches Gericht hat entschieden: Christina Block muss den drei Kindern, die beim Vater in Dänemark leben, Unterhalt zahlen. Allerdings deutlich weniger, als von ihrem Ex-Mann gefordert.

spiegel.title: Langlauf: Victoria Carl spricht über Rückkehr nach Dopingsperre
spiegel.description: Ein falscher Hustensaft zerstörte beinahe die Karriere von Olympiasiegerin Victoria Carl. Nun kehrt sie zurück, spricht erstmals ausführlich über ihre 18 Monate lange Zwangspause – und sagt, was sie ändern will.

spiegel.title: Elif Eralp nach SPIEGEL-Enthüllung: Der entscheidenden Frage weicht sie aus
spiegel.description: Elif Eralp will nach der SPIEGEL-Enthüllung über ihre Angst vor Terrorsympathisanten entschlossen wirken. Sie verspricht, gegen Gewalt und Kriminalität vorzugehen. Und was ist mit den Radikalen in den eigenen Reihen?

spiegel.title: Kanada und EU wollen Beziehung auf »höchstmöglicher Ebene«
spiegel.description: Die EU und Kanada beraten auf einem gemeinsamen Gipfel über eine engere Zusammenarbeit. Doch wie soll die künftige Verbindung heißen? Darüber gibt es EU-intern Streit. Jetzt wurde eine Formulierung gefunden.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde tritt ab, Elif Eralp äußert sich, Friedrich Merz bereist Asien
spiegel.description: Friedrich Merz hat auf seiner Asienreise Gebäck im Gepäck. EZB-Chefin Christine Lagarde tritt vorzeitig zurück. Und die Berliner Linkenpolitikerin Elif Eralp äußert sich nach den SPIEGEL-Enthüllungen. Das ist die Lage am Donnerstagabend.

spiegel.title: Regierungsbildung in Israel: Nun hat Isaac Herzog die Wahl
spiegel.description: Bei den israelischen Parlamentswahlen konnte kein Lager eine klare Mehrheit erringen. Nun muss Präsident Herzog entscheiden, wen er mit der Regierungsbildung beauftragt.

spiegel.title: Audi-Aufsichtsrat beruft Sondersitzung ein
spiegel.description: Seit Tagen steht Audi-Boss Gernot Döllner für seinen Auftritt mit US-Präsident Donald Trump in der Kritik. Nun hat Audi eine Aufsichtsratssitzung angesetzt.

spiegel.title: US-Präsident über Norwegen: Tourismusverbände machen sich über Donald Trumps »Scheißhaus«-Spruch lustig
spiegel.description: Bilder von spektakulären Toilettenhäuschen und sensationelle Naturaufnahmen: Norwegen reagiert lässig auf die jüngsten Attacken von Donald Trump. Der hatte sich beleidigt zur Aussage verstiegen, das Land sei kacke.

spiegel.title: Himemaru Rice Cracker: Unternehmen ruft verunreinigten Snack zurück
spiegel.description: Die 98-Gramm-Packung Himemaru Rice Cracker wurde in fast allen Bundesländern verkauft. Nun ruft der Hersteller den Snack zurück.

spiegel.title: Kreis Lörrach: Fußgängerin und Kind sterben bei Unfall mit Lkw
spiegel.description: Eine 62-Jährige ging mit einem Kinderwagen hinter einem Lastwagen entlang, als dieser zurücksetzte. Die Frau und das Kind starben noch an der Unfallstelle.

spiegel.title: »Sächsische Separatisten«-Prozess: Drei Haftbefehle aufgehoben
spiegel.description: Mehrere mutmaßliche Mitglieder der »Sächsischen Separatisten« sind auf freiem Fuß. Nach zwei Jahren U-Haft wurden gegen drei von acht Angeklagten der Neonazigruppe die Haftbefehle aufgehoben.

spiegel.title: Berlin – Linke: Hendrikje Klein zur Präsidentin des Abgeordnetenhauses gewählt
spiegel.description: Die neue Präsidentin des Berliner Abgeordnetenhauses ist eine Linke. Das Parlament hat Hendrikje Klein in seiner ersten Sitzung nach der Berlinwahl ins Amt gewählt. Nicht nur mit Stimmen von Rot-Grün-Rot.

spiegel.title: Hongkong: Ministerin tritt nach Hochhausbrand zurück
spiegel.description: Beim verheerenden Brand eines Hochhauskomplexes in Hongkong starben 168 Menschen, Tausende wurden obdachlos. Eine Untersuchung sieht eine Mitverantwortung der Regierung. Nun hat die Wohnbauministerin ihr Amt niedergelegt.

spiegel.title: Condor einigt sich mit Piloten
spiegel.description: Die 1000 Condor-Pilotinnen und -Piloten haben sich mit der Fluggesellschaft auf einen langfristigen Tariffrieden verständigt. Sie verzichten gegen Beschäftigungszusagen unter anderem für zwei Jahre auf Gehaltserhöhungen.

spiegel.title: Russland: Deutsche EU-Politiker loben Gesprächsversuch mit Wladimir Putin
spiegel.description: Der finnische Präsident und der norwegische Regierungschef haben mit Russlands Machthaber Wladimir Putin telefoniert. Politiker von CDU, Grünen und FDP unterstützen den Anruf – das ist überraschend.

observador.title: Três municípios unem-se para avançar com Metrobus
observador.description: Protocolo aprovado pela Câmara da Amadora envolve também a Carris e a TML. O projeto prevê um corredor dedicado entre Algés e a estação da Reboleira.

observador.title: Governo prepara novas regras de acolhimento de idosos
observador.description: Apenas 649 pessoas acolhidas em dezembro de 2025. O Governo quer ampliar uma resposta social com 35 anos mas de "aplicação muito residual".

observador.title: As notícias das 17h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer

observador.title: BCE. Lagarde sai para usar a "voz" na defesa da "verdade"
observador.description: Sem confirmar que vai para o WEF, Christine Lagarde justificou saída antecipada do BCE com o desejo de ter uma "voz" livre numa fase em que, considera, a "verdade" é diariamente posta em causa.

observador.title: A nova vida da marca Kukas, 60 anos de joias depois
observador.description: A arquiteta Filipa Fortunato lidera a nova fase da marca de joalharia e peças de interior, lançada pela pioneira do design contemporâneo, que morreu este ano, aos 97 anos.

observador.title: Deputado atropela criança. Investigação ainda em aberto
observador.description: Carlos Silva Santiago, do PSD, admitiu estar embriagado no momento da colisão, em 2024. Dois anos depois, o processo continua. Porquê a demora? O advogado Miguel Matias é o convidado.

observador.title: Trump diz que eleições no Brasil são "uma vergonha"
observador.description: O Presidente dos EUA comentou a vitória de Lula com 51,7%, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro, refugiado nos EUA, recusa reconhecer o resultado e ameaça contestá-lo nos tribunais.

observador.title: Idoso atirado a poço: casal julgado em Beja na terça-feira
observador.description: Os dois arguidos, de 40 anos, estão acusados de roubo, sequestro agravado e homicídio qualificado. A vítima foi mantida viva na bagageira do carro durante horas.

observador.title: Durán sem suspensão imediata pode defrontar Gil Vicente
observador.description: O CD abriu processo disciplinar ao avançado colombiano, mas sem efeito imediato. Marco Silva confirmou a convocatória para o duelo com o Gil Vicente.

observador.title: Morreu a avó: como ajudar as filhas a viver o luto
observador.description: Uma ouvinte perdeu a mãe há dois meses e meio, de forma inesperada. As filhas, de 10 e 7 anos, vivem o luto de maneiras opostas, e ela guardou o seu numa caixa. Como ajudá-las, e a si própria?

observador.title: BPP: primeiros pagamentos a credores comuns
observador.description: Comissão liquidatária ordenou pagamentos a 400 credores em dois momentos. No total, 80 milhões serão distribuídos, equivalendo a 8,4% dos créditos reconhecidos.

observador.title: Von der Leyen agradece a Lagarde por reforçar o euro
observador.description: A presidente da Comissão Europeia e o líder do Eurogrupo reagiram ao anúncio da saída antecipada de Christine Lagarde do BCE, prevista para fevereiro de 2027.

observador.title: Rangel destaca "sinal político" do aumento da verba do MNE
observador.description: Paulo Rangel defendeu o crescimento de 7,7% no orçamento da política externa para 2027 numa audição parlamentar sobre o OE2027, destacando aumentos consecutivos nas receitas de impostos.

observador.title: Chuva. Uma frente dia 5 e a primeira grande tempestade a 10?
observador.description: Os modelos coincidem: há duas grandes tempestades no Atlântico, uma atinge-nos para a semana com uma frente a outra vem na nossa direção e pode ser a primeira da época. Mas primeiro pode vir o frio.

observador.title: Queixa à PGR pede investigação ao diretor da PSP e Governo
observador.description: Denúncia de 23 páginas, apresentada por um cidadão com advogado, cobre as quatro intervenções policiais de 15 e 25 de outubro em Lisboa e no Porto e pede urgência na preservação de prova.

observador.title: Julgamento de Nuno Lopes marcado para janeiro de 2027
observador.description: Ator português diz-se inocente no caso em que é acusado de violação e "satisfeito" com a definição de uma data para o julgamento com júri, marcado para 11 de janeiro em Nova Iorque.

observador.title: Porto. Detidos três jovens suspeitos de agressões violentas
observador.description: O grupo de cerca de 10 jovens atacou o morador com murros, pontapés e arma branca na zona de Miragaia. A vítima ficou em perigo de vida.

observador.title: Amadora entrega 48 chaves de habitações com renda acessível
observador.description: As habitações, no Cerrado da Mira, acolhem 56 pessoas selecionadas entre cerca de 500 candidaturas. A construção custou 6,9 milhões, pagos a 100% pelo PRR.

nyt.title: Nvidia Chief, Jensen Huang, Is Seen as Target of Chinese Spy Plot
nyt.description: A Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Jensen Huang was found to be passing intelligence to Beijing. President Trump was briefed and took no action.

nyt.title: U.S. GDP Increased 3.4% in Third Quarter
nyt.description: The economy grew 3.4 percent in the third quarter, the fastest pace in a year. Strong spending and growth contrast with the poor marks many voters are giving the economy.

nyt.title: Inflation Accelerated in October, PCE Index Shows
nyt.description: The Personal Consumption Expenditures index picked up in September, according to data released a day after the Federal Reserve’s decision to hold interest rates steady.

nyt.title: The Fed Risks Falling Behind in its Inflation Fight
nyt.description: Federal Reserve officials are expected to restart rate increases in December, but the cadence of additional moves will depend on the data.

nyt.title: Third-Party Spoilers, Long Fueled by Both Parties, Could Matter This Year
nyt.description: The other Dan Sullivan in Alaska has drawn the most attention, but both parties are quietly trying to use little-known candidates in other battlegrounds to siphon votes, too.

nyt.title: The Red States That Could Decide the Senate
nyt.description: Democrats need to flip four Republican-held Senate seats to regain the majority, but some of their targets are in states President Trump won by double digits in 2024. Our election data reporter Evan Reynolds explains just how difficult that might be.

nyt.title: Four Scenarios for How the Midterms Could Go
nyt.description: Expectations are cresting for Democrats, and some kind of wave seems likely, but so much will depend on a few close Senate races.

nyt.title: After 28 Years Walking the Globe, Karl Bushby Is Almost Home
nyt.description: Karl Bushby has walked 31,000 miles, crossing some of the world’s harshest landscapes. He plans to reach his mother’s house in England next week.

nyt.title: Trump and His Aides Helped Bolsonaro Flee Brazil and Enter U.S.
nyt.description: President Trump ensured Flávio Bolsonaro, who lost a presidential election in Brazil and faces multiple criminal investigations there, could enter the United States, U.S. officials said.

nyt.title: Ilhan Omar Investigation Involves New Scrutiny of Long-Disputed Marriage
nyt.description: Several current and former law enforcement officials said an Obama-era investigation found some evidence that Ms. Omar had entered into a sham marriage with a man suspected of being her brother.

nyt.title: Spain Crash Investigators Focus on Train Traffic Controllers’ Role
nyt.description: After the country’s second major rail disaster in a year, Spaniards were confronting questions about the safety of their once-vaunted rail system.

nyt.title: I Can Hear Everything
nyt.description: The world can be tough to navigate with one working ear. Even now with two, I still face challenges.

nyt.title: Campaign for California’s Billionaire Tax Pins Its Hopes on Influencers and Social Media
nyt.description: Supporters of a California wealth tax are short on cash and are relying on cheaper campaign methods to get their word out.

nyt.title: 2026 Midterm Election Ballot Measures: What Races We’re Watching
nyt.description: More than 140 statewide ballot measures will go before voters during the midterms. Here are the races we’re watching.

nyt.title: Suddenly, Empathy Isn’t So Toxic
nyt.description: Deport immigrants? Oh yes. But not this guy.

nyt.title: Why Are We Having Less Sex? Ask a Pornographer.
nyt.description: Erika Lust wants to excite you.

nyt.title: Stacking Ballots
nyt.description: A tale of political intrigue from Alaska.

nyt.title: Russian Strike on Ukrainian Train Station Kills 14
nyt.description: A deadly strike was a grim reminder that despite a rare local cease-fire around the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, other communities remained under fire.

elpais.title: La maquinista del Iryo de Urda intentó desbloquear su tren dos veces sin éxito y buscó asistencia de su empresa antes de la colisión
elpais.description: La conductora contactó con el centro de Adif en Atocha, donde se vivían momentos de confusión, y con el de su propia compañía

elpais.title: El consejero delegado de Iryo advirtió de los problemas del sistema LZB en sus trenes tres semanas antes del accidente de Urda
elpais.description: Fabrizio Favara alertó en el Senado de las desconexiones del sistema de señalización de la línea Madrid-Sevilla y los problemas para reanudar la marcha

elpais.title: ¿Por qué chocaron los trenes? Tres fallos catastróficos que han costado 69 vidas
elpais.description: Se apuntan al menos tres problemas encadenados. Repasamos lo que sabemos del accidente y las principales incógnitas

elpais.title: El Rey pide que se determine “cómo y por qué” ha sucedido la catástrofe de Urda y medidas para que “no vuelva a suceder”
elpais.description: Felipe VI y Letizia Ortiz visitan el Hospital de Toledo, donde se atiende a la mayoría de heridos por la colisión de trenes que ha causado al menos 69 muertos

elpais.title: Muere la exministra Fátima Báñez, que viajaba en uno de los trenes siniestrados en Urda
elpais.description: La titular de Empleo entre 2011 y 2018 estuvo vinculada en los últimos años a la CEOE

elpais.title: Sánchez asegura que se “reforzará la seguridad” ferroviaria para evitar nuevos accidentes
elpais.description: Puente comparecerá el martes 3 de noviembre a petición propia en la Diputación Permanente del Congreso tras la solicitud de varios socios

elpais.title: Feijóo apunta a las “responsabilidades políticas” de Puente por el segundo accidente mortal de la alta velocidad en nueve meses
elpais.description: El líder de la oposición no pide de forma explícita la dimisión del ministro, pero deja entrever que él lo habría cesado: “Yo sé lo que haría si fuera el presidente del Gobierno”

elpais.title: La mirada de corresponsales extranjeros sobre el accidente de trenes
elpais.description: Periodistas de todo el mundo están en Urda para contar lo que ha pasado y prevenir en países que van a invertir en alta velocidad sobre los riesgos de esta tecnología

elpais.title: Accidente de trenes en Toledo: última hora y reacciones en directo | El PP pide la comparecencia de Sánchez en el Congreso y considera “insuficiente” la de Puente
elpais.description: La autoridad de accidentes ferroviarios rectifica y mantiene en 69 | CC OO pide el cese de Óscar Puente por culpar a un operador del accidente de Urda | Sánchez asegura que se “reforzará la seguridad” ferroviaria para evitar nuevos accidentes

elpais.title: Rodrigo se durmió, perdió el tren y se libró del accidente; ahora busca a su primo desaparecido
elpais.description: Rodrigo Hernández, de origen mexicano, tenía previsto tomar el AVE siniestrado, pero no se despertó a tiempo. Aún busca a un familiar entre las víctimas

elpais.title: Noche al límite en la morgue de Toledo para albergar los cuerpos de los fallecidos: “Están buscando forenses”
elpais.description: En el Instituto de Medicina Legal de Toledo, cuya capacidad se ha ampliado con carpas y contenedores frigoríficos, se practican las autopsias de las víctimas mortales

elpais.title: El Gobierno amplió el contrato de mantenimiento del sistema de seguridad de la línea Madrid-Sevilla un día antes del accidente
elpais.description: El Consejo de Ministros del martes aprobó un incremento de 11,5 millones a la empresa que se encarga de los sistemas de control del AVE a Andalucía

elpais.title: Yo viajaba en ese tren
elpais.description: Antonio Jiménez Barca, periodista de EL PAÍS, se encontraba en la cafetería del AVE en el momento en que impactó en el Iryo. Relata los primeros momentos de caos

elpais.title: Sin noticias de José San Emeterio, el hombre que viajaba con Trece, el perro devuelto a su mujer
elpais.description: La familia continúa buscando al sevillano desde que un reloj inteligente alertó de que su ubicación estaba sobre las vías

elpais.title: Continúan las labores de rescate tras el accidente de trenes de Toledo: cientos de efectivos y psicólogos para “cuando se quiten el uniforme”
elpais.description: Un día después de la tragedia de Urda, en la zona cero, el caos y el pánico han dado paso al silencio que acompaña al trabajo sin descanso de los servicios de rescate y la maquinaria pesada para encontrar a las víctimas

elpais.title: Cómo ayudar a las víctimas tras una catástrofe como el accidente de tren de Urda: “El psicólogo debe estar desde el minuto uno, como un bombero”
elpais.description: Los precedentes muestran que las catástrofes con un componente humano son más difíciles de superar que las naturales y que la gente es más solidaria de lo que se cree

elpais.title: Catástrofes inasumibles
elpais.description: El segundo choque mortal de dos trenes de alta velocidad en menos de un año es un golpe a la confianza de los ciudadanos en el Estado

elpais.title: Se acabó la campaña
elpais.description: Mientras se determina si el fallo fue estructural o humano, a muchos no se nos quitará el miedo fundado a coger unos trenes que llevan más de 100 muertos en menos de un año

republika.title: Precipita elicottero italiano in Bosnia: possibili vittime
republika.description: L’incidente vicino a Brcko. Secondo le notizie diffuse dai media locali, almeno tre militari sarebbero morti e una decina feriti. Non ancora rivelata la nazionalità

republika.title: Il tuo nuovo tatuaggio? Lo firma casa Rembrandt
republika.description: Nella casa museo del pittore, ad Amsterdam, un gruppo di tatuatori riprodurrà sulla schiena di un giovane olandese una delle incisioni più complesse del maestro. Ma non solo: chiunque potrà prenotarsi fino al 7 novembre per farsi tatuare un particolare dai disegni del pittore

republika.title: Cortei, la strategia del Viminale: isolare i violenti e contenere con moderazione chi protesta
republika.description: Alla vigilia delle manifestazioni di domani in 50 piazze il ministro dell’Interno Piantedosi riunisce questori e prefetti: “Gli allarmi ci sono, ma gestiremo anche l’imprevedibilità”. Confermato l’uso del fermo preventivo

republika.title: È ancora Corto Maltese. Igort firma il nuovo graphic novel dell’eterno marinaio
republika.description: Hugo Pratt voleva che il suo eroe continuasse a esistere. Per questo uno dei maggiori autori di fumetti italiani ha deciso di rischiare, disegnando una nuova avventura, “La casa delle orchidee bianche”: «È come incidere la cover di un brano perfetto. Ma bisogna saper osare»

republika.title: Marco Steiner: Hugo Pratt lasciava sempre una porta aperta
republika.description: Lo storico collaboratore del Maestro racconta come è nato il nuovo albo. Che cerca di dare un nome a una misteriosa “lei”

republika.title: La crociera dei super ricchi anti-Trump bloccata per il caro carburanti: “Fermi in Cambogia per la guerra in Iran”
republika.description: Il viaggio della Villa Vie Odissey doveva durare tre anni e mezzo e toccare 150 Paesi. L’idea era stata lanciata poco prima della rielezione alla Casa Bianca di Donald, come un mezzo – ristretto a persone facoltose – per stare lontani dall’America per tutta la durata della sua presidenza

republika.title: Caso Siher, i togati del Csm: “Chiediamo l’apertura di una pratica a tutela della gip di Milano”
republika.description: Si tratta di una pratica a tutela per Tiziana Landoni, gip presso il Tribunale di Milano, in relazione alle dichiarazioni del Presidente del Consiglio sul provvedimento di non convalida del fermo di Youssef Siher

republika.title: Camicie nere e foto del Duce alla cena per la Marcia su Roma con militanti FdI, Lega e vannacciani
republika.description: In una trattoria alle porte di Milano l’evento con cento persone in occasione del 104esimo anniversario promosso nell'ambiente di Futuro Nazionale

republika.title: Mps, l'assemblea boccia la fusione con Mediobanca e le due Ops su Banco Bpm e Banca Generali
republika.description: L’assemblea respinge la fusione con Piazzetta Cuccia: i no al 63,65%. Lovaglio: "Da Intesa cambio di rotta. In 4 anni mantenute le promesse e segnato anche da calcio d'angolo"

republika.title: Manovra, Meloni torna ad attaccare l’Istat. Crosetto: in 2 anni neanche un euro in più per la difesa
republika.description: Le affermazioni della premier nell’anticipazione del nuovo libro di Bruno Vespa

republika.title: Israele, “soldi del Qatar per aumentare affluenza arabi”: commissione elettorale chiede un’inchiesta
republika.description: Aperta un’indagine su “gravi sospetti di interferenze straniere ostili” nel voto del 27 ottobre. Doha respinge le accuse. Il giallo dello Shin Bet: “Aveva elementi concreti prima delle elezioni ma non è intervenuto”

republika.title: Sugar e Plastic tax, sette anni di rinvii: sono tasse fantasma. E provano la debolezza dei governi
republika.description: Esistono dal 2019 ma non sono mai state applicate. Anche il governo Meloni ha certificato la nona proroga al luglio 2027. La storia delle due imposte emblema delle difficoltà a decidere e scontentare

republika.title: L’Italia scende in piazza: da Torino a Napoli, tutti i cortei di domani
republika.description: Le manifestazioni previste, città per città. Per evitare disordini sono stati deviati alcuni percorsi. Sotto la Mole vietati caschi e passamontagna, a Roma limitati gli ingressi a Termini e Colosseo

republika.title: Le madri dei liceali: "Anche noi in piazza contro la violenza sui nostri figli”
republika.description: L’iniziativa lanciata da una docente di Matematica dell’università di Bologna per lo sciopero del 30 ottobre: “I nostri ragazzi hanno paura del futuro e della polizia, per questo noi mamme saremo con loro. Ci vestiremo di rosso per poterci riconoscere”

republika.title: Disastro in Spagna, ritrovata una delle tre italiane disperse. Le altre due non si trovano ancora
republika.description: Questa mattina, una di loro ha contattato il nostro Consolato a Madrid. Le altre due sono un’italo-venezuelana e l’altra italo-argentina. Il bilancio delle vittime sale a 69

republika.title: Serbia, il sistema Vucic si sgretola: nel mirino i giudici della repressione
republika.description: Dopo la vittoria della Lista degli studenti, la procura generale dispone verifiche negli 87 tribunali del Paese sui casi di repressione e sulle violazioni dei diritti. Nel mirino i magistrati accusati di aver protetto il sistema di potere del leader nazionalista

republika.title: Decreto flussi, falla nel sistema per badanti: quasi tutte donne ma a fare richiesta sono uomini
republika.description: La Filcams Cgil denuncia un sistema delle quote «fallimentare» che alimenta lavoro irregolare e sfruttamento. Anomalie anche nelle provenienze e nella distribuzione territoriale. Il sindacato chiede canali stabili e maggiori tutele

republika.title: Kimi, un’attesa da togliere il fiato: a 2200 metri tra tequila e cappellini per la festa
republika.description: Nell’aria rarefatta dell’altitudine di Città del Messico, Antonelli sta per coronare un sogno che l’Italia attende da 73 anni

npr.title: US and Japan agree to establish a Japanese facility for joint missile production
npr.description: The announcement Wednesday is the latest action by the allies, who have repeatedly expressed alarm over China's growing assertiveness in Asia.

npr.title: China elevates a military general to the Politburo and seeks to strengthen party discipline
npr.description: This move comes about a year before President Xi Jinping is expected to secure his fourth five-year term.

npr.title: Greetings from Baghdad, where Agatha Christie's old home presents its own mystery

phys-org.title: Shrinking bat populations can weaken ecosystem benefits even while species remain widespread
phys-org.description: Bats promote the health of ecosystems in many ways. Insect-eating species help regulate insect populations, including agricultural and forest pests. In tropical and subtropical regions, nectar-feeding and fruit-eating bats pollinate plants and disperse seeds, supporting plant reproduction and forest regeneration.

phys-org.title: Werewolf mice, ghostly frogs and cockroach zombies: The animal versions of our Halloween horrors

But you may be surprised to hear that in the animal world, there are many real-life creatures with tendencies similar to those of the fictional characters in our Halloween nightmares.

phys-org.title: Africa's water availability sometimes goes untapped

phys-org.title: New catalyst builds proton highways to tackle a long-standing hurdle in green ammonia synthesis

Today, however, the same method consumes about 1% of global energy and contributes more than 1% of annual anthropogenic CO₂ emissions.

phys-org.title: How stealth partisan outlets exploit trust in local journalism
phys-org.description: New research from Carnegie Mellon University's Kenneth C. Griffin School of Computer Science found that partisan media operations spent millions of dollars on social media ads ahead of key elections to promote pink slime websites masquerading as local news sources to sway voters with their content.

Detecting this light and mapping its fluctuations provide valuable insights into the age and composition of the universe.

Nobu of the Japan Agency for Marine-Earth Science and Technology (JAMSTEC) and Satoshi Nakagawa of Kyoto University has for the first time isolated and cultivated two strains of Heimdallarchaeia, a group of archaea that are among the closest known archaeal relatives of eukaryotes—the organisms that include humans and other animals, as well as plants and fungi.

phys-org.title: Rainfall can travel from mountain slopes to rivers far faster than expected in mountain catchments
phys-org.description: Researchers at University of Tsukuba have found that river responses to rainfall can reach rivers and appear as runoff much more rapidly than previously assumed in mountainous regions. phys-org.title: Ancient charcoal remains provide clues about Neanderthal camp organization
phys-org.description: Usually, people associate archaeological studies with bones, pottery and primitive tools, but archaeologists often find other clues about how ancient people lived hidden throughout a site. A new study, published in the Journal of Paleolithic Archaeology, focuses on bits of charcoal and their spatial organization to get a glimpse of Neanderthal life in Abric Romaní, an ancient rock shelter near Barcelona.

phys-org.title: How universities can help deliver global biodiversity goals
phys-org.description: "Taking Action for Nature" was the theme of CoP 17, the UN Biodiversity Conference 2026, which is drawing to a close in Yerevan, Armenia. A new analysis of African national biodiversity strategies and action plans shows how academic and research institutions can respond to this theme and help translate scientific evidence into taking action for nature.

phys-org.title: Enormous 'Cat's Tail' tells of cosmic collision 63 light-years away
phys-org.description: Sixty-three light-years from Earth, in the small, faint constellation known as Pictor (which is Latin for "painter"), there lies a strange structure that has puzzled astronomers for the last two years. Nicknamed the "Cat's Tail," this dark feature stretches across an abyss of space about a thousand times the average distance between Earth and the sun.

phys-org.title: New tropical protea flowers expand floriculture opportunities across Hawaiʻi
phys-org.description: Researchers at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa College of Tropical Agriculture and Human Resilience (CTAHR) have bred new "tropical" pincushion protea (Leucospermum) hybrids that bloom near sea level, reducing local reliance on imported flowers.

undark.title: The FDA Wants to Pull Its Approval of a Drug. It’s Not So Easy.
undark.description: In 2021, the FDA was on the fence about whether to approve a new treatment for a rare form of vasculitis. After an advisory committee narrowly recommended approval, the agency greenlit the drug, Tavneos, and it started making its way into clinics. After uncovering evidence of what it says is data manipulation in the original trial, the agency wants to rescind the approval. But it’s not so easy.

undark.title: Podcast: The Entanglements Series Finale
undark.description: Welcome to the last installment of Entanglements, at least for the foreseeable future. In this final episode, hosts Brooke Borel and Anna Rothschild are joined by Undark editor-in-chief Tom Zeller Jr. to talk about the show’s successes, failures, and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is There a Population Crisis?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Michael Geruso, an associate professor of economics at the University of Texas at Austin, and Jennifer Dowd, a professor of demography and population health at the University of Oxford, about population trends and fertility rates.

undark.title: Podcast: Which Animals Are Conscious?
undark.description: This week on the show, our hosts talk to Heather Browning, a philosopher at the University of Southampton in the U.K, and Deb Brown, a philosopher and the  director of the Critical Thinking Project at the University of Queensland in Australia, about which animals feel pain and more.

undark.title: Podcast: Is ADHD Actually a Disorder?
undark.description: On Entanglements this week: Barbara Franke, a professor of molecular psychiatry at Radboud University in the Netherlands, and Edmund Sonuga-Barke, a developmental psychologist and a professor at King’s College London discuss whether ADHD should be considered a disorder.

undark.title: Podcast: Should We Put AI-Enabled Tech in Our Brains?
undark.description: Welcome to Season 3 of Entanglements! In our first episode, we discuss neural implants and AI with Judy Illes, a professor of neurology and neuroethics at the University of British Columbia, and Joseph J. Fins, a physician scientist and medical ethicist at Weill Cornell Medicine in New York.

undark.title: Engineering Animals to Grow Human Organs — But Not Human Minds
undark.description: Chimeras, or animals with human cells and tissues, are not new, and researchers have long used them to gain insights into diseases and even as a potential source of transplantable organs. But the research brings up thorny ethical questions regarding animal rights and the moral status of chimeric creatures.

undark.title: AI-Driven Biology Is Only as Good as the Data Beneath It
undark.description: Opinion | The biotech and pharma industries are pouring billions of dollars into AI-driven drug discovery and development. But the genomic data used to train AI models are often incomplete, contain errors, or lack contextual information — a quality issue that threatens to slow the pace of biological research.

undark.title: In Italy, What Earth Can Tell Us About Extraterrestrial Life
undark.description: Photo Essay | From sampling hydrothermal vents and abandoned mines to lab experiments that replicate Mars’ atmosphere, scientists are using what we know about life on Earth to understand how it may exist on other worlds. Italy, it seems, provides particularly fertile ground for such explorations.

undark.title: The Evolving Quest to Build Life in a Lab
undark.description: Scientists are trying to create new life, whether to understand how biology first developed on Earth, or design new cells from scratch.  But life hasn’t happened — at least not yet. And questions around safety, as well as what even constitutes life in the first place, continue to swirl.

proj-syn.title: Can Bond Vigilantes Prevent the Next Debt Crisis?

proj-syn.title: A Wealth Tax Would Harm California

Since wealth is mobile, those who stand to lose the most will simply leave, taking their future income-tax payments with them.

proj-syn.title: A Future for Europe’s Youth
proj-syn.description: The current generation of young Europeans possesses freedoms, material resources, opportunities to travel, and technological capabilities beyond anything previous generations could have imagined. Their demands, however, are strikingly simple: decent schools, secure jobs, affordable homes, and the possibility of raising a family.

proj-syn.title: A Tale of Two Chinas
proj-syn.description: China’s economy is deeply unbalanced, with a battered real-estate sector, weak consumption, and stark regional disparities coexisting with dynamic tech and export sectors. But provided that political stability is maintained, China could continue to be a global powerhouse even as hundreds of millions of its citizens remain poor.

proj-syn.title: Sino–American Stability?
proj-syn.description: Delegates at the Bund Summit in Shanghai largely agreed that the US-China relationship could be entering a new, less contentious chapter, although many were more interested in what the post-Trump era will mean for Sino-American ties. But perhaps the most heartening sign for the future was the honest exchange of views.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Winter of Discontent
proj-syn.description: Although it is true that European integration has always been forged through crisis, the continent’s postwar story was largely one of incremental responses to relatively manageable challenges. Today, the European Union is facing multiple, interrelated problems that challenge its very raison d’être.

proj-syn.title: How Students Dethroned Serbia’s Strongman
proj-syn.description: Following the ouster of Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán after 16 years in power earlier this year, the world has once again witnessed the merits of “old-school” campaigning. In toppling their own country's strongman, Serbia's new student-led opposition offers important lessons for those defending democracy elsewhere.

proj-syn.title: What a US-China AI Safety Channel Needs
proj-syn.description: Addressing AI safety risks depends on close collaboration between the two leading AI powers, and the establishment of an incident-reporting channel is just a small step in this direction. But success will require that the US and Chinese governments actually understand what is happening under their own noses.

proj-syn.title: The Authoritarian Logic of Selective Privacy
proj-syn.description: Around the world, governments are increasingly deciding who gets privacy and who is denied it, a double standard that turns a fundamental democratic right into a privilege. US President Donald Trump’s administration is a prime example, shielding ICE agents from scrutiny while expanding surveillance of immigrants and protesters.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Chapter in the Anti-Authoritarian Playbook
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s renewed democratic confidence must now be matched by institutional and structural reforms and a willingness to build coalitions beyond the left. Recent democratic outcomes in Hungary and Serbia offer useful lessons.

proj-syn.title: Another Crash Landing for Brazil’s Economy?
proj-syn.description: Brazil’s floating exchange rate, high foreign-exchange reserves, strong commodity exports, and debt denominated predominantly in its own currency reduce its exposure to a balance-of-payments crisis. Nonetheless, continued fiscal deterioration under President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will carry high domestic costs.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Make-or-Break Moment Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: US President Donald Trump has not only abandoned Ukraine and America’s European allies, but has increasingly sided with Russian President Vladimir Putin. To preserve their sovereignty, Europeans must remain united in the face of outside pressure, which in turn requires managing political threats from within their borders.

proj-syn.title: Middle Powers Can Lead on AI Safety
proj-syn.description: With the United States showing no interest in regulating AI, middle powers have an opportunity to take the lead on governance. By banding together, these countries could condition market access on meeting a common set of safety requirements and explore joint investment in technical capacity.

proj-syn.title: Lula Killed the Donroe Doctrine
proj-syn.description: In attempting to disentangle the United States from the rest of the world and retreat into a seemingly controllable hemispheric stronghold, Donald Trump's Latin America strategy had fared better than the rest of his foreign policy. But following a defeat for the far right in Brazil, his project now looks dead in the water.

proj-syn.title: The Wrong Way to Compare Economic Size
proj-syn.description: At the European Central Bank’s annual research conference, Paul Krugman concluded that, when it comes to “weaponized interdependence,” the EU is more powerful than both the US and China. But his reliance on PPP-adjusted GDP as a way to smooth out the volatility of nominal exchange rates ignores the even greater swings in PPP data.

proj-syn.title: Public Control for a Purposeful Economy
proj-syn.description: As more governments recognize the need for greater public control over economic outcomes, they must be careful to define the concept well. What ultimately matters is not ownership, but the state’s capacity to steer economic activity toward strategic objectives in the service of the common good.

proj-syn.title: Rethinking Sustainable Livelihoods From the Ground Up
proj-syn.description: In regions where economic activity has long revolved around fossil-fuel extraction, ensuring a just transition requires developing alternative livelihoods that account for each community’s specific needs. Regional endowment funds could be a useful vehicle for funding these local initiatives.

crunchbase.title: Series B Funding Is Up, But Fewer Deals Are Getting Done
crunchbase.description: Crunchbase data shows that so far this year, investors have poured around $48 billion into financings around the Series B stage, the highest tally in years. Yet round counts are below year-ago levels and are on track for a multiyear low. We take a look at the data.

crunchbase.title: Jumbo Series A Rounds Hiding The Real Squeeze On Seed Startups
crunchbase.description: AI megarounds are masking a shrinking Series A market, leaving seed founders facing higher revenue expectations and longer timelines despite larger seed checks. To improve their chances, MGV's Marc Schröder says, founders should size their seed funding around Series A milestones.

crunchbase.title: The Crunchbase Tech Layoffs Tracker

crunchbase.title: Exclusive: Numeracle Raises $28M To Keep Legitimate Business Calls From Spam Label

crunchbase.title: The Invisible Graph: How Companies Grow Revenue And Still Lose Value
crunchbase.description: Revenue growth does not guarantee a larger exit, as declining valuation multiples can outweigh operating gains and reduce enterprise value. Guest author Itay Sagie suggests that founders and boards should track valuation alongside financial performance, model the effects of delaying a sale, and begin M&A preparation while the business is strong and buyer interest is favorable.

crunchbase.title: From Monk To Startups: One Founder’s Unusual Path To Building Government Software
crunchbase.description: After living as a monk while managing Graves’ disease, a former Facebook engineer left Big Tech to pursue meaningful work, eventually founding government software startup FSH Technologies which aims to improve processes such as school food services and public records management through the use of artificial intelligence.

crunchbase.title: Crunchbase Data Shows Q3 Robotics Startup Funding Jumps 185% As US And China Lead Physical AI Push
crunchbase.description: Venture funding to robotics startups has soared in 2026, with the bulk of investment going to companies based in China and the U.S., Crunchbase data shows. All told, global venture funding to robotics startups totaled $9.9 billion in Q3, more than double the $4.3 billion invested in Q3 2025, per Crunchbase data.

crunchbase.title: Your AI Agents Need A Chief Operating Officer, Too
crunchbase.description: Scaling AI agents requires treating them like employees in regulated roles, with written rules, clearly defined responsibilities and a named human manager accountable for their performance. Guest author Rick Folgmann, COO at Get Covered, tells companies they should start with tasks governed by established rules, adjust autonomy to each workflow’s risks, and regularly review results before expanding agents’ authority.

crunchbase.title: Some Observations About Anthropic’s IPO Filing

However, in a preliminary once-over, we highlight some of the more intriguing disclosures.

crunchbase.title: When Traction Becomes Personal Exposure: What The Joonko Guilty Plea Means For Founders
